newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee stable vs fwd dlr, spot down on RBI.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee stable vs fwd dlr, spot down on RBI.

text.p: The Indian rupee was stable against the forward dollar in late morning Tuesday trade but continued to slide in the spot market on central bank purchases of the US currency, dealers said.
They said October dollars quoted a premium of 92/94 paise against Monday's close of 91/94.
Dealers said they did not expect forward premiums to rise much further immediately.
"I think current levels are all right, given that call money seems to have settled at 9.0-10.0 percent," said a dealer.
"The Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) spot-dollar purchases should release rupees into the system over the next few days and ease liquidity leading to lower call money rates," he said.
"We see little chance of premiums going up much in the short-term unless importers start covering forward exposures."
Dealers said the rupee dropped to 35.835 per dollar in spot deals as RBI dollar purchases put it under pressure.
The rupee opened Tuesday at 35.780/785, unchanged from Monday's close.
Dealers described the RBI's dollar purchases as "heavy".
"They (RBI) would have bought more than they did yesterday," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
Dealers estimated RBI's Monday purchases at around $150 million. The rupee fell to an intraday low of 35.80 on Monday before retracing to 35.780/785 against its opening quotes of 35.745/755.

"Given the firming up of call rates, the RBI may have decided to step up its intervention in the forex market," said another dealer. "Earlier it was worried about the effects of its intervention on domstic monetary supply expansion."
Call money has been above 9.0 percent since last Friday after being stuck below 1.0 percent through most of April.
Dealers however said demand from corporates remained poor.
"Basically, it is RBI which is driving the market and maybe a few banks which have been caught short," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Otherwise, there is little demand for dollars."
In latest deals, the dollar was quoted 35.825/835 rupees.
